solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Email edited to make speech better (10)

indicatorNotes.edited: an edited text has had its parts changed and moved around

blocks.note: EMAIL, edited
to orate is to make a speech

annotation.surface: Someone polishes an email so that it says what they mean more clearly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective at the end of the surface, but it is the verb: to better something is to improve it.
annotation.definitionFit: Ameliorate is a formal synonym for improve, the verb sense of better, as in bettering one's lot.

entries.clue: In times past, back end of the chancel (4)

indicatorNotes.In: the letters sit in the words that follow
indicatorNotes.back: the letters are read back, right to left

blocks.note: timES PAst holds E-S-P-A, read here from right to left

annotation.surface: A historian notes how the east end of a church was laid out long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back end' looks like one phrase for the rear of the building, but 'back' is the instruction and 'end of the chancel' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The apse is the rounded recess that closes off the east end of a church's chancel.

entries.clue: Eastern block united by Blake’s last poem (7)

indicatorNotes.last: take only the final letter of Blake

blocks.note: E = Eastern
to clog is to block
U = united, as in football club names
last letter of BLAKE

annotation.surface: A literary note links a poem to the Eastern Bloc, united by William Blake's final work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eastern block' hints at the Soviet Eastern Bloc; here it is split into E plus a verb for obstruct.
annotation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, as in Virgil's Eclogues.

entries.clue: Brooding overture, perhaps including piano (13)

indicatorNotes.including: the outer phrase takes the letter into itself

blocks.note: an overture is an example of an intro section of a piece
p = piano, soft in music; goes inside after INTROS

annotation.surface: A music critic describes a dark, moody overture that features the piano.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brooding' looks like an adjective for the overture; it is a noun here, the act of brooding, which is what introspection is.
annotation.definitionFit: Introspection is brooding: turning one's thoughts inward on oneself.

entries.clue: Scarcity of high earners close to Leeds (8)

indicatorNotes.high: high as in intoxicated, so the letters are all over the place
indicatorNotes.close to: take the final letter of Leeds

blocks.note: anagram fodder
last letter of LEEDS
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: An economist remarks that big earners are hard to find near Leeds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High earners' reads as one phrase about salaries; 'high' is split off to scramble the earners.
annotation.definitionFit: Rareness is scarcity: the quality of being seldom found.

entries.clue: Tool for gripping underwear husband discarded (5)

indicatorNotes.discarded: the husband is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: thongs are skimpy underwear
H = husband; removed from THONGS

annotation.surface: Someone reaches for a tool to pick up the underwear a husband has thrown aside.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the husband discarded the underwear; in the wordplay it is the husband's H that is discarded.
annotation.definitionFit: Tongs are a tool with two arms for gripping and lifting things.

entries.clue: Trick WC Fields initially rejected (4)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of Fields
indicatorNotes.rejected: sent back, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: first letter of FIELDS, which ends up in front once everything is turned round
a WC is a loo, here read backwards

annotation.surface: A prank pulled by comedian W.C. Fields was turned down at first.
annotation.walkthrough: W.C. Fields, the American comedian, is split in two: WC is the toilet and Fields gives only its F.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to trick someone into believing something is to make a fool of them.

entries.clue: Something repellent in paintings — blood (7)

blocks.note: oils are oil paintings
blood = family, kin

annotation.surface: A gallery-goer finds something repugnant in paintings: blood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repellent' suggests something disgusting; the sense needed is water-repellent.
annotation.definitionFit: Oilskin is cloth treated with oil to repel water, used for rain gear.

entries.clue: What Gavin does for gain gets discouraged (5,5)

blocks.note: GAVIN drops its middle letter V to become GAIN
to become disheartened

annotation.surface: A man called Gavin does something for profit and ends up disheartened.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic riddle: take the heart (middle letter) out of GAVIN and you have GAIN.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who loses heart gets discouraged, and GAVIN literally loses its heart.

entries.clue: Rent a place on the Adriatic (5)

blocks.note: a rent is a tear, as in a torn sleeve
a Croatian port city on the Dalmatian coast

annotation.surface: A holidaymaker plans to rent somewhere on the Adriatic coast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a verb about letting property; it is the noun meaning a tear.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a rent in cloth is a tear, and the Croatian port Split sits on the Adriatic.

entries.clue: Can openers belt cricket shots? (4-5)

blocks.note: a belt is a ring round something
a pull is a cricket shot to the leg side

annotation.surface: Can the opening batsmen hit hard cricket shots?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can openers' reads as a question about the opening batsmen who can hit; it is the tabs on drink cans. The question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Ring-pulls are the metal tabs used to open drink cans.

entries.clue: He’s number two in this organisation (8,5)

annotation.definition: He’s number two in this organisation

blocks.note: the surface wants a deputy; He is the chemical symbol for helium, atomic number 2
not a company but the chart that organises the elements by number

annotation.surface: Someone points out the deputy in a company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'He' is not a man but the symbol for helium, atomic number 2, and the organisation is the chart that arranges the elements.
annotation.definitionFit: The periodic table organises the elements, with helium second.

entries.clue: Shots of tennis players crushed by medical crises (6,7)

blocks.note: ground = crushed, as coffee
a stroke is a medical emergency

annotation.surface: Photographs show tennis players struck down by health emergencies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shots' suggests photographs; it is tennis shots, and the players are only part of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ground strokes are tennis shots played after the ball bounces.

entries.clue: Cook’s ingredients inventory grows exponentially (5,5)

blocks.note: a shop's inventory is its stock
to cube a number raises it to the power three

annotation.surface: A kitchen's supply of ingredients keeps multiplying out of control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grows exponentially' is jargon for rapid growth; here it is the arithmetic of raising to a power.
annotation.definitionFit: Stock cubes are dried blocks of stock that cooks use as ingredients.

entries.clue: Breaking lock, step inside? (8)

indicatorNotes.inside: the step goes within the lock

blocks.note: a lock of hair is a tress
a pas is a dance step; goes inside TRES…S

annotation.surface: A burglar breaks the lock and steps into the house.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a trespass, while 'lock' and 'step' also give TRESS and PAS; 'lock' is hair, not a door fitting.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: forcing a way past a lock and walking into property without permission is exactly the offence the whole clue describes.

entries.clue: Elasticity of university head’s clothing (6)

indicatorNotes.clothing: the head wraps round the university letter like clothes

blocks.note: bonce is British slang for the head
U = university; goes inside BO…NCE

annotation.surface: Someone remarks on the stretchy fabric of a college principal's outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'University head' reads as a vice-chancellor; the head is a separate word, the slang bonce.
annotation.definitionFit: Bounce is springiness, the elasticity of a ball or a fabric.

entries.clue: Dwelling trendies refurbished (8)

indicatorNotes.refurbished: a refurbished place has been rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Fashionable types have done up their home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dwelling' reads as a noun for a home; it is the adjective, as in living somewhere.
annotation.definitionFit: Resident means dwelling in a place, as in a resident doctor.

entries.clue: Clerical office bunch regularly turning rude (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so the letters are taken at every second step

blocks.note: bUnCh gives U and C, the second and fourth letters, then turned round
racy = risqué, rude

annotation.surface: A parish office full of people who keep becoming rude.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Office' is not a workplace but a post held, here that of a curate.
annotation.definitionFit: A curacy is the office or post of a curate, an assistant priest.

entries.clue: Loot bag, bolted on top (7)

indicatorNotes.on top: in a down answer, RAN goes above SACK

blocks.note: bolted = ran off
a sack is a bag

annotation.surface: A thief grabs a bag of loot and runs off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loot' looks like a noun for the stolen goods in the bag; it is the verb, to plunder.
annotation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to loot it, searching and stealing.

entries.clue: Puzzle’s case to become more brutish (8)

blocks.note: be = become, exist
wilder = more savage

annotation.surface: A puzzle's solution makes someone more animal.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words and it is an instruction to grow more brutish; the clue says that is the case with this word for puzzle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to bewilder someone is to leave them thoroughly confused.

entries.clue: Act to keep police resolute (7)

indicatorNotes.to keep: the act holds the police inside it

blocks.note: a deed is an act
CID, the UK Criminal Investigation Department; goes inside DE…ED

annotation.surface: Legislation to retain the police force is firmly backed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Act' reads as a law passed by Parliament; it is a deed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone decided in their views is firm and resolute, not wavering.

entries.clue: Keen to dine on one’s own? (13)

annotation.definition: Keen to dine on one’s own?

blocks.note: eager to eat, which sounds like an ordinary appetite
the surface says alone; the meaning is on one's own kind

annotation.surface: Someone happy to eat alone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On one's own' suggests solitude; read it as eating one's own kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Cannibalistic means eating members of one's own species.

entries.clue: One comes round every year without delay (5)

indicatorNotes.comes round: the one goes round the outside

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards
p.a. = per annum, each year; goes inside A…CE

annotation.surface: An annual visitor arrives promptly every year.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Comes round every year' suggests something annual, like a birthday; it splits into the container instruction and PA.
annotation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb, from 'at a pace': things moving apace go swiftly, without delay.

entries.clue: Craft device for turning hard wood (4)

blocks.note: H = hard, as on pencils
elm is a wood

annotation.surface: A woodworker's lathe for turning hardwood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Craft device for turning' suggests a lathe; the craft is a boat and the turning is steering.
annotation.definitionFit: A helm is a boat's wheel or tiller, used to turn the vessel.

entries.clue: Flap on underwear: popular idea (9)

indicatorNotes.on: the flap is placed after the rest

blocks.note: a bra is underwear
in = fashionable, popular
to flap a hand is to wave

annotation.surface: A designer has a winning thought: a flap on underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flap' looks like a fold of cloth on the garment; it is the verb for waving.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal: a sudden clever thought that arrives out of nowhere, the kind a designer would call an idea.

entries.clue: Romeo has left Harry for Mark (5)

indicatorNotes.has left: Romeo has gone from the word

blocks.note: to harry someone is to pester them persistently
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet; it leaves the end of the word

annotation.surface: Romeo has dumped Harry for someone called Mark.
annotation.walkthrough: The three names look like a love triangle; Harry is the verb meaning to badger, and Mark is the noun for an emblem.
annotation.definitionFit: A badge is a mark or emblem, of rank or membership.

entries.clue: Religious adherent’s request to be heard (4)

indicatorNotes.to be heard: the word is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: to seek something is to ask for it

annotation.surface: A believer asks for a hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Request to be heard' reads as asking for a hearing; it is the sound of a synonym for request.
annotation.definitionFit: A Sikh is a follower of Sikhism, the faith founded in the Punjab.

entries.clue: Pagans had The Omen distributed (10)

annotation.definitionNote: Heathendom is a collective noun for the heathen world, so plural 'Pagans' fits.

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Heathens were handed copies of the horror film The Omen.
annotation.walkthrough: The Omen, a horror film about the Antichrist, fits the pagan theme but is only letters here.
annotation.definitionFit: Heathendom is the world of heathens: pagans taken together.
